Consider the following PR description:
choose does not broadcast index array appropriately (Trac #925)
_Original ticket http://projects.scipy.org/numpy/ticket/925 on 2008-10-03 by @teoliphant, assigned to unknown._

The advertised behavior of choose(choices, sequence_of_arrays) is that the choices array and all the arrays in the sequence must be broadcastable to the same shape which is the shape of the output. 

However, NumPy does not look at the shape of the choices array, only the sequence_of_arrays. 

This requires an adaptation of the code in PyArray_Choose function in C.   Probably the easiest thing is to construct a MultiIterator object to handle the broadcasting internal to that function, construct the output, and then fill appropriately.


</pr_description>

static PyObject *
PyArray_Choose(PyArrayObject *ip, PyObject *op, PyArrayObject *ret,
               NPY_CLIPMODE clipmode)
{

    int n, elsize;
    intp i, m;
    char *ret_data;

    mps = PyArray_ConvertToCommonType(op, &n);

               NPY_CLIPMODE clipmode)
{
    intp *sizes, offset;
    int n, elsize;
    intp i, m;

    PyArrayObject **mps, *ap;
    intp *self_data, mi;
    int copyret=0;

    mps = PyArray_ConvertToCommonType(op, &n);

    sizes = (intp *)_pya_malloc(n*sizeof(intp));
    if (sizes == NULL) goto fail;

    ap = (PyArrayObject *)PyArray_ContiguousFromAny((PyObject *)ip,
                                                    PyArray_INTP,
                                                    0, 0);
    if (ap == NULL) goto fail;

    /* Check the dimensions of the arrays */
    for(i=0; i<n; i++) {
        if (mps[i] == NULL) goto fail;
        if (ap->nd < mps[i]->nd) {
            PyErr_SetString(PyExc_ValueError,
                            "too many dimensions");
            goto fail;
        }
        if (!PyArray_CompareLists(ap->dimensions+(ap->nd-mps[i]->nd),
                                  mps[i]->dimensions, mps[i]->nd)) {
            PyErr_SetString(PyExc_ValueError,

            goto fail;
        }
        sizes[i] = PyArray_NBYTES(mps[i]);
    }

       did not work (see ticket #925).

    ap = NULL;

import numpy as np

def check(cond, msg):
    if not cond:
        raise AssertionError(msg)

# 1. Index (2,1), choices (3,) -> (2,3)

r = a.choose([np.array([10,20,30]), np.array([40,50,60])])
check(r.shape == (2,3) and np.all(r == [[10,20,30],[40,50,60]]), "case1")

# 2. Index (3,), choices each (1,3) -> (1,3)
a = np.array([0,1,0])
r = a.choose([np.array([[10,20,30]]), np.array([[40,50,60]])])
check(r.shape == (1,3) and np.all(r == [[10,50,30]]), "case2")

# 3. Index (2,1,1), choices (3,) -> (2,1,3)? actually broadcast (2,1,1) and (3,) -> (2,1,3)
a = np.array([[[0]],[[1]]])
c0 = np.array([10,20,30]); c1 = np.array([40,50,60])
r = a.choose([c0, c1])
check(r.shape == (2,1,3), "case3 shape")
check(np.all(r[0] == [[10,20,30]]) and np.all(r[1] == [[40,50,60]]), "case3")

# 4. Same shape as before, (2,3) index and (2,3) choices
a = np.array([[0,1,0],[1,0,1]])
r = a.choose([np.array([[10,20,30],[40,50,60]]), np.array([[100,200,300],[400,500,600]])])
check(r.shape == (2,3), "case4")
check(np.all(r == [[10,200,30],[400,50,600]]), "case4 vals")

# 5. out parameter with broadcast shape
a = np.array([[0],[1]])
out = np.empty((2,3), dtype=int)
r = a.choose([np.array([10,20,30]), np.array([40,50,60])], out=out)
check(r is out, "case5 is out")
check(np.all(out == [[10,20,30],[40,50,60]]), "case5 vals")

# 6. mode wrap/clip
a = np.array([[-1, 2]])
r = a.choose([np.array([10,20]), np.array([30,40])], mode='wrap')
check(np.all(r == [[30,10]]), "case6 wrap")  # -1 wraps to 1 -> 30, 2 wraps to 0 -> 10
r = a.choose([np.array([10,20]), np.array([30,40])], mode='clip')
check(np.all(r == [[10,40]]), "case6 clip")  # -1->0->10, 2->1->40
try:
    a.choose([np.array([10,20]), np.array([30,40])], mode='raise')
    raise AssertionError("case6 raise should fail")
except ValueError:
    pass

# 7. scalar index with array choices
r = np.array(1).choose([np.array([10,20]), np.array([30,40])])
check(r.shape == (2,) and np.all(r == [30,40]), "case7")

# 8. zero-length choose raises
try:
    np.array(1).choose([])
    raise AssertionError("case8 should raise")
except ValueError:
    pass

# 9. object refcount behavior (from regression test)
class Obj(object):
    def __init__(self): pass
obj = Obj()
arr1 = np.zeros((5,1), dtype=object)
arr2 = np.zeros((5,1), dtype=object)
import sys
base = sys.getrefcount(obj)
arr1[...] = [obj]*5
arr2[...] = [obj]*5
arr3 = np.array([[0],[1],[0],[1],[1]], int).choose(arr1, arr2)
# these reference counts are tricky; just make sure it doesn't crash and values are right
check(np.all(arr3.ravel() == obj), "case9 vals")
del arr3
del arr2
del arr1
print("All broadcast/edge tests passed")
EOF"}
